reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the creator endorses HedgeConnect, says he will invest and leave a link, and invites viewers to join despite acknowledging referral commission. The promoted offer ties token purchases and lending or staking participation to daily passive income, stated interest, and projected token-price gains; the creator's risk warnings do not undo that direct solicitation.

opening.argument: Judge, the speaker does not certify this investment as safe. He calls the pitch "false advertisement and false Hope" and warns that lending platforms can disappear (ASR_0005). He also says the promised outcome is speculative, not guaranteed (ASR_0013), and tells worried viewers to stay away (ASR_0016). His decision to risk a small amount himself is compatible with a cautionary review; it does not turn those explicit warnings into a promise to viewers.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's purchase quote establishes his own intention, not a guarantee to viewers. The link is an invitation to inspect an investment he repeatedly qualifies, and the $45 figure is described as a target rather than an assured return (ASR_0010). Judge the invitation alongside his direct instruction to stay away if losing money is a concern (ASR_0016).

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Warnings do not erase the solicitation. After saying he will buy coins, the speaker says he will leave a link for this investment (ASR_0015), then explicitly tells viewers they can get coins through the description and acknowledges referral commission (ASR_0016). The reviewed offer also presents lending as a way to earn daily passive profit (ASR_0007). The concern is the combined promotion of that investment mechanism, not whether he promises a risk-free outcome.

opening.argument: Judge, the structure here is an examination of a platform, not a sales presentation. The title asks whether it is legitimate or a scam (TITLE_0001). The speaker says he is going through its white paper (ASR_0004), challenges its claim to be safest (ASR_0004), and calls its "groundbreaking" trading bot a red flag (ASR_0011). Showing viewers what the project claims while questioning those claims is review and education, even when the reviewer considers a personal purchase.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution isolates the purchase, link and price target from the review around them. The speaker identifies the projected prices as ambitious and explicitly says they are not guaranteed (ASR_0010). A review can include a personal decision and a way to inspect the subject without adopting every claim in its white paper; here he says those claims may never be carried out as written (ASR_0013).

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The critical commentary is real, but the speaker goes beyond explaining the white paper. He says he likes the idea and will invest (ASR_0013), says he will provide a link for a platform he believes could work (ASR_0010), and ends by inviting viewers to get coins through the description (ASR_0016). The review format therefore does not fully account for his affirmative invitation to participate.

opening.argument: Judge, a disclosed referral link is not by itself proof of deceptive solicitation. The speaker acknowledges that he could receive commission but says he would rather risk his own money first (ASR_0016). He discusses buying coins for himself (ASR_0015), while telling viewers concerned about their money to stay away (ASR_0016). Those statements establish an optional purchase and a disclosed commercial interest; they do not establish that a viewer paid him, surrendered credentials, or received a guaranteed return.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that a link and a price target appear. But the speaker describes the price increase as uncertain (ASR_0010), and his commission disclosure makes the referral interest visible rather than concealing it (ASR_0016). Those excerpts do not show a completed deposit, a credential request, or a promised payout to a viewer. His own proposed purchase is not evidence that anyone else obtained a return.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed victim payment or credential request is not necessary to recognize the offer being promoted. The project presents lending coins for daily passive profit and lists daily interest payments (F0028). The speaker says he will buy coins (ASR_0015), offers viewers a way to get them through the description, and acknowledges commission (ASR_0016). Disclosure limits concealment, but it does not change the substance of that investment invitation.
